summary: Virginia Range lookout south of Virginia City, built by the Forest Service in 1932, passed to BLM in 1963, closed in 1970 and destroyed in 1971; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: One-story building about 14 feet square and 12 feet high (1951 Coast and Geodetic Survey description)
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service; transferred to the Bureau of Land Management in 1963
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1971 per the 2012 California-Nevada chapter report; the Nevada lookout list also marks the site Gone

staffing.status: Last staffed 1970; named lookouts George Merkle (1933) and Iola Ferguson (1944-1951)

events.note: District ranger H.I. Snider recommended a lookout to the Forest Service
Forest Service station finished in late 1932; Washoe County built the access road; $800 from the Forest Service and about $400 from the Clarke-McNary act
George Merkle named as lookout in August 1933; earliest named lookout found
Iola Ferguson worked the lookout every season from 1944 to 1951 except one
Transferred from the Forest Service to the Bureau of Land Management
Closed in 1970 because of smog (Nevada State Journal, July 1970); last staffed 1970 per the 2012 report
Destroyed in 1971 per the 2012 report; the sources give no cause

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.org lists the site in Storey County. The Forest Lookouts history places it in the Virginia Range east of Washoe Valley and says Washoe County built its road. The sources read give no county line, so the story does not state a county and the record keeps the list's Storey.

sources.title: California - Sierra and Nevada Chapter 2012 Annual Report

notes_for_editor: The firelookout.org list and the SummitPost plateau guide describe the same McClellan Peak area, but the guide never names the lookout, so tying the plateau's cell towers to the lookout site is an inference. No source describes remains or current access. The 1931 and 1932 items say Virginia range; the 1951 item says Washoe range. Staffing comes from newspaper items, so a gap between named lookouts is not evidence the tower stood empty.
